evals.prompt: Give me a quick read of arXiv 2403.05131 — I want the tl;dr before deciding if it's worth a deep dive.
evals.expected_output: A structured summary under exactly the seven required headers, in order, grounded only in the paper's actual text, followed by a write-back of the Quick read section to the discussion note.
expectations: Output uses the seven headers in order: Research gap / question(s), Background, Key assumptions, Findings, Conclusions, Shortcomings, Future directions
Checks .prioris/papers/arxiv/2403.05131.md for a cache before calling any fetch tool
If a section genuinely doesn't apply, says so briefly rather than fabricating content
Appends or updates a 'Quick read' section in .prioris/discussions/arxiv/2403.05131.md using the same seven headers
Sets read_at in the discussion note's frontmatter if not already set
Writes the quick-read entry automatically, without asking the user whether to save or overwrite it

evals.prompt: Search for a paper about vision transformers for medical image segmentation and quick-read it for me.
evals.expected_output: Runs a Search/Select step like discuss (ranked candidate list, confirm which paper) before fetching, picking a provider consistent with the plugin's subject-matter routing rule and stating which provider it used.
expectations: Presents a ranked list of candidates (provider, title, authors, year, abstract snippet) before fetching full text
Confirms with the user which single paper to open, unless one is already unambiguous
Does not fetch full text during the search/select step
States or implies which provider (arxiv vs europepmc) it searched, consistent with the plugin's routing rule rather than silently picking one

evals.prompt: Quick summary of this paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09876
evals.expected_output: Extracts the canonical arXiv identifier from the URL before calling any tool, then goes straight to fetch (skipping search/select since the paper is already named), and produces the standard seven-header summary.
expectations: Does not pass the raw URL to any prioris-mcp tool call
Extracts identifier 2401.09876 from the URL before fetching
Skips the search/select step since a specific paper was already named
Produces the same seven-header structure as a directly-named-id request

evals.expected_output: Recognizes the paper already has a recorded Quick read section and presents that cached section directly, without re-fetching or re-summarizing.
expectations: Checks .prioris/discussions/arxiv/2403.05131.md for an existing 'Quick read' section before calling any MCP tool
Does not call research_arxiv_fetch_full_text, research_arxiv_parse_full_text, or any other prioris-mcp tool
Presents the cached seven-header content rather than regenerating a new summary
Does not rewrite or append to the discussion note, since nothing changed

evals.prompt: Refetch arXiv 2403.05131 and give me a fresh quick read — the paper's been revised since we last looked at it.
evals.expected_output: Skips both the discussions cache short-circuit and the papers cache reuse, fetches fresh from the MCP server, regenerates the seven-header summary from the new text, and overwrites both cached files.
expectations: Does not present the existing cached 'Quick read' section as-is, despite one already existing
Does not reuse .prioris/papers/arxiv/2403.05131.md as-is; calls research_arxiv_fetch_full_text and research_arxiv_parse_full_text fresh
Overwrites .prioris/papers/arxiv/2403.05131.md with the newly fetched content
Regenerates the seven-header summary from the newly fetched text and replaces the 'Quick read' section in the discussion note
